title: Alternative Site Selection
text: Planned sampling locations sometimes turn inaccessible field — private land, dangerous terrain, logistical constraints. Rather dropping locations entirely, ss_alt_sites() finds environmentally similar replacement sites elsewhere study area, overall design keeps covering range conditions. approach: Generate pool candidate sites across study area (ss_alt_candidates()) Optionally exclude candidates close inaccessible sites, replacements spatially distinct (ss_alt_filter_buffer()) Compute environmental similarity inaccessible site every candidate (ss_alt_similarity()) Rank select similar candidates alternatives (ss_alt_rank())

title: Alternative Site Selection
text: ss_alt_similarity() supports three distance metrics target site candidate, converted [0, 1] similarity score (1 = identical): Mahalanobis (default): accounts correlation covariates via population covariance matrix. robust covariates correlated, needs enough candidates estimate stable covariance matrix. Euclidean: simple geometric distance range-normalization. Faster, ignores covariate correlation. Gower: handles mix continuous categorical covariates via per-variable normalized differences.

title: Alternative Site Selection
text: ss_alt_filter_buffer() removes candidate within min_distance inaccessible site, similarity computed. avoids picking “alternatives” really just adjacent original problem location (e.g. inaccessible area).

title: Alternative Site Selection
code: library(soilsampling) library(terra)  set.seed(11)  nr <- 40 nc <- 40  r <- rast(nrows = nr, ncols = nc, xmin = 0, xmax = 1000, ymin = 0, ymax = 1000, nlyrs = 3) names(r) <- c("dem", "slope", "ndvi")  xy <- xyFromCell(r, seq_len(ncell(r))) values(r)[, "dem"] <- 100 + 20 * sin(xy[, 1] / 150) + rnorm(ncell(r), 0, 3) #> Warning: [readValues] raster has no values values(r)[, "slope"] <- abs(cos(xy[, 2] / 120) * 8 + rnorm(ncell(r), 0, 1)) values(r)[, "ndvi"] <- pmin(pmax(0.5 + 0.3 * cos(xy[, 1] / 200 + xy[, 2] / 250) +   rnorm(ncell(r), 0, 0.05), -1), 1)  # A few "inaccessible" sites needing alternatives inaccessible <- data.frame(   x = c(200, 500, 800),   y = c(200, 500, 800) ) inaccessible #>     x   y #> 1 200 200 #> 2 500 500 #> 3 800 800

title: cLHS + Random Forest Optimization
text: Conditioned Latin hypercube sampling (cLHS) gives design environmentally representative, representativeness predictive accuracy. Wadoux et al. (2019) showed cLHS baseline can improved specific prediction task directly optimizing sample locations Random Forest’s cross-validated prediction error. package implements idea two-stage workflow: cLHS baseline: generate representative starting design (ss_clhs_sample()) Simulated annealing refinement: iteratively swap sample points minimize Random Forest MSE (ss_rf_optimize()) ss_rf_size() runs stages end--end produces comparison plots.

title: cLHS + Random Forest Optimization
text: candidate design, ss_rf_mse() fits Random Forest kk-fold cross-validation, predicting one covariate (“response”) others, returns mean squared error averaged across folds. Lower MSE means design’s points informative predicting variable rest.

title: cLHS + Random Forest Optimization
text: ss_rf_optimize() starts cLHS baseline repeats, n_iterations: Replace one randomly chosen sample point randomly chosen point currently design Compute candidate design’s RF MSE Accept swap improves MSE, probabilistically accept worse swap probability exp⁡(−Δ/T)\exp(-\Delta / T) (Metropolis criterion) Cool temperature: T←T×cooling_rateT \leftarrow T \times \text{cooling\_rate} Early iterations (high temperature) tolerate worse moves, allowing search escape local optima; later iterations (low temperature) accept improvements, converging refined design. best design seen point tracked returned, regardless search ends .

title: KL Sample Size Optimization
text: Conditioned Latin hypercube sampling (cLHS) widely used select environmentally representative sampling locations, leaves one question open: many samples enough? samples fail represent environmental variability study area; many waste field laboratory resources. Malone et al. (2019) proposed answering using Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence: run cLHS range candidate sample sizes, measure well sample’s distribution matches population’s distribution across covariates, pick smallest sample size reaches target level representativeness. vignette walks ss_kl_size() building blocks: ss_load_rasters(), ss_kl_divergence(), ss_kl_optimize(), ss_kl_save_plots().

what: KL Divergence Between Population and Sample
title: KL Sample Size Optimization
text: numeric covariate, population candidate sample binned histograms breaks. KL divergence variable : KL=∑iOilog⁡(OiEi) KL = \sum_i O_i \log\left(\frac{O_i}{E_i}\right) OiO_i sample’s density bin ii EiE_i population’s density bin. ss_kl_divergence() averages across numeric covariates, giving single divergence score per sample: lower better (representative).

what: From Divergence to Optimal Sample Size
title: KL Sample Size Optimization
text: ss_kl_optimize() repeats sequence sample sizes (min_samples max_samples, step_size increments), running n_replicates independent cLHS draws size. mean KL divergence per size fit exponential decay curve: KL(n)=b1e−kn+b0 KL(n) = b_1 e^{-kn} + b_0 optimal sample size smallest nn cumulative proportion achievable improvement, max⁡(KL)−KL(n)max⁡(KL)−min⁡(KL), \frac{\max(KL) - KL(n)}{\max(KL) - \min(KL)}, reaches probability_threshold (default 0.95) — .e. point diminishing returns.

title: Maxvol Optimal Design Sampling
text: maxvol algorithm D-optimal design method selecting sampling locations maximizing determinant (volume) feature submatrix. Unlike traditional probability-based sampling, maxvol takes deterministic optimal design approach selects locations maximum diversity feature space. method particularly effective : Features explain soil variability: Terrain attributes correlate soil properties Deterministic selection preferred: Non-random, reproducible point placement samples available: Optimal coverage minimal sampling effort Model-based inference planned: Kriging machine learning predictions

title: Maxvol Optimal Design Sampling
text: Given matrix 𝐀\mathbf{} size m×nm \times n (mm represents locations nn represents features), maxvol algorithm selects kk rows form submatrix 𝐀̂\hat{\mathbf{}} approximately maximum determinant: 𝐀̂=arg⁡maxsubmatrix|det⁡(𝐀k)| \hat{\mathbf{}} = \arg\max_{\text{submatrix}} |\det(\mathbf{}_k)| Geometrically, determinant represents volume nn-dimensional parallelepiped spanned row vectors. Maximizing volume ensures selected locations maximal diversity feature space.

title: Maxvol Optimal Design Sampling
text: maxvol algorithm implements D-optimal experimental design, minimizes determinant covariance matrix parameter estimates. practical terms, D-optimal designs: Spread samples across feature space Minimize correlation sample locations feature space Maximize information parameter estimation

title: Maxvol Optimal Design Sampling
text: Feature Matrix Construction: Create matrix 𝐀\mathbf{} row represents location columns represent features (elevation, slope, TWI, etc.) Normalization (optional): Standardize features zero mean unit variance Rectangular Maxvol (rect_maxvol): Initialize kk random rows Compute coefficient matrix 𝐁=𝐀⋅𝐀̂−1\mathbf{B} = \mathbf{} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{}}^{-1} Iteratively swap rows maximize volume Apply distance constraints specified Point Selection: Selected row indices correspond sampling locations

title: Maxvol Optimal Design Sampling

text: soilsampling package provides methods designing soil sampling schemes. implements: Simple Random Sampling: Uniform random selection sampling locations Stratified Random Sampling: Random sampling within compact geographical strata Spatial Coverage Sampling: Purposive sampling stratum centroids optimal coverage Maxvol Optimal Design Sampling: Feature-based sampling using D-optimal experimental design Composite Sampling: Sampling equal-area strata combined samples Validation Metrics: Assess stratification quality coverage efficiency distance statistics KL Sample Size Optimization: Determine optimal cLHS sample size via Kullback-Leibler divergence cLHS + Random Forest Optimization: Refine cLHS design simulated annealing minimize RF prediction error Alternative Site Selection: Find environmentally similar replacement sites inaccessible sampling locations

title: soilsampling: Soil Sampling Design Methods
text: Feature-based sampling using D-optimal experimental design maximize diversity: maxvol algorithm selects locations maximize determinant (volume) feature submatrix, ensuring maximum diversity feature space. particularly effective : - Features explain soil-forming factors - need deterministic (non-random) point selection - want optimal coverage samples
code: # Create a grid with terrain features strata <- ss_stratify(study_area, n_strata = 100, n_try = 5) cells_sf <- strata$cells  # Add terrain features (in practice, extract from DEM) coords <- st_coordinates(cells_sf) cells_sf$elevation <- coords[,2] + rnorm(nrow(coords), 0, 5) cells_sf$slope <- abs(rnorm(nrow(coords), 5, 2)) cells_sf$twi <- rnorm(nrow(coords), 8, 1.5)  # Select 20 optimal samples based on features samples <- ss_maxvol(   cells_sf,   n = 20,   features = c("elevation", "slope", "twi"),   min_dist = 5,        # Minimum distance between samples   normalize = TRUE,    # Normalize features to equal scales   add_coords = TRUE    # Include coordinates as features )  ss_plot_samples(samples)

Use ss_kl_optimize() underlying optimization without raster /O, ss_kl_divergence() compute divergence arbitrary population sample.
code: library(terra)  predictors <- rast("data/predictors.tif")  result <- ss_kl_size(   predictors,   min_samples = 10,   max_samples = 200,   step_size = 10,   n_replicates = 10,   output_dir = "outputs"   # optional: writes CSVs and plots )  result$optimal_sample_size result$plot_cdf

code: predictors <- rast("data/predictors.tif")  result <- ss_rf_size(   predictors,   n_samples = 100,   n_iterations = 500,   seed = 123,   output_dir = "outputs"   # optional: writes CSVs and comparison plot )  result$comparison_table result$improvement   # % MSE reduction vs. the cLHS baseline

title: soilsampling: Soil Sampling Design Methods
text: Evaluate uniformly cells distributed across strata: Output metrics: - CV (Coefficient Variation): Lower values indicate uniform distribution - Min/Max Ratio: Ratio smallest largest stratum (1.0 = perfect equality) - Gini Coefficient: Standard inequality measure (0 = perfect equality) - Efficiency Score: Qualitative assessment (Excellent/Good/Fair/Poor) Comparing stratification methods:
code: # Create stratification strata <- ss_stratify(study_area, n_strata = 25, n_try = 5)  # Assess coverage efficiency efficiency <- ss_coverage_efficiency(strata) print(efficiency) # Regular stratification strata_regular <- ss_stratify(study_area, n_strata = 20, n_try = 5)  # Equal-area stratification strata_equal <- ss_stratify(study_area, n_strata = 20,                              equal_area = TRUE, n_try = 5)  # Compare efficiency eff_regular <- ss_coverage_efficiency(strata_regular) eff_equal <- ss_coverage_efficiency(strata_equal)  cat("Regular CV:", eff_regular$cv, "\n") cat("Equal-area CV:", eff_equal$cv, "\n") # Equal-area should have much lower CV (< 0.05 vs 0.15-0.30)

title: soilsampling: Soil Sampling Design Methods
text: Compute distance cells samples stratum centroids: Output (per stratum): - Mean, SD, min, max, median distances centroid - Helps identify dispersed compact strata - Default: squared distances (consistent MSSD metric) Use cases: - Compare different stratification runs (n_try values) - Verify equal-area maintains compactness - Identify strata unusual geometry
code: # For stratification dist_summary <- ss_distance_summary(strata) print(dist_summary)  # For samples (works with coverage or stratified samples) samples <- ss_coverage(strata) dist_samples <- ss_distance_summary(samples, actual_distance = TRUE) print(dist_samples)

text: package uses pure R implementations k-means algorithms: Transfer Algorithm (default): Standard k-means iteratively transfers cells nearer cluster centers. Creates compact potentially unequal-sized strata. Swop Algorithm (equal_area = TRUE): Modified k-means swaps cells clusters maintain equal sizes optimizing compactness. algorithms minimize Mean Squared Shortest Distance (MSSD) cells assigned cluster centroids.

title: soilsampling: Soil Sampling Design Methods — soilsampling-package
text: soilsampling package provides methods designing soil sampling schemes including spatial coverage sampling, simple random sampling, stratified random sampling, composite sampling. package uses sf spatial operations require Java sp package.

title: soilsampling: Soil Sampling Design Methods — soilsampling-package
text: package implements three main sampling approaches: Simple Random Sampling (ss_random()): Selects sampling locations uniformly random within study area. Stratified Random Sampling (ss_stratified()): Divides study area compact strata samples randomly within stratum. Spatial Coverage Sampling (ss_coverage()): Places samples centroids compact geographical strata optimal spatial coverage. stratification based k-means clustering described Walvoort et al. (2010). Two k-means algorithms available: Transfer algorithm: Standard k-means creates compact strata potentially unequal sizes. Swop algorithm: Creates compact strata equal size, useful composite sampling.

title: soilsampling: Soil Sampling Design Methods — soilsampling-package
text: Stratification: ss_stratify() - Create spatial strata using k-means Sampling: ss_random() - Simple random sampling ss_stratified() - Stratified random sampling ss_coverage() - Spatial coverage sampling (centroids) ss_coverage_equal_area() - Coverage sampling equal-area strata ss_composite() - Composite sampling equal-area strata Visualization: ss_plot() - Plot stratification samples ss_plot_samples() - Plot sampling points Utilities: ss_to_sf() - Convert results sf object ss_to_data_frame() - Convert results data frame ss_summary() - Get summary statistics ss_n_strata() - Get number strata ss_n_samples() - Get number samples ss_area() - Get stratum areas ss_relative_area() - Get relative stratum areas

title: soilsampling: Soil Sampling Design Methods — soilsampling-package

code: library(soilsampling) library(sf)  # Load or create study area study_area <- st_read("study_area.shp")  # Option 1: Direct coverage sampling samples <- ss_coverage(study_area, n_strata = 50, n_try = 10)  # Option 2: Create strata first, then sample strata <- ss_stratify(study_area, n_strata = 50, n_try = 10) samples <- ss_coverage(strata)  # Visualize ss_plot(strata, samples = samples)  # Export coordinates coords <- ss_to_data_frame(samples) write.csv(coords, "sampling_points.csv")

title: soilsampling: Soil Sampling Design Methods — soilsampling-package
text: Spatial coverage sampling (ss_coverage()): Best model-based inference (kriging). Provides optimal spatial coverage interpolation. Stratified random sampling (ss_stratified()): Best design-based inference. Provides valid probability samples ensuring coverage. Simple random sampling (ss_random()): Use prior stratification desired. Valid design-based inference. Composite sampling (ss_composite()): Use samples physically combined analysis reduce costs.

text: function computes several metrics assess uniformity: Coefficient Variation (CV): Ratio standard deviation mean. Gini Coefficient: Standard inequality measure economics. 0 = perfect equality, 1 = maximal inequality. Lower values indicate better uniformity. title: Maxvol Optimal Design Sampling — ss_maxvol
text: maxvol algorithm selects sampling locations finding submatrix feature matrix approximately maximum determinant (volume). Geometrically, maximizes volume parallelepiped spanned selected feature vectors, ensuring sampled locations maximal diversity feature space. algorithm based D-optimal experimental design particularly effective : Features explain main soil-forming factors want deterministic (non-random) point selection need optimal coverage samples Feature Selection: Terrain features typically used include: Elevation Slope Aspect Topographic Wetness Index (TWI) Closed depressions Flow accumulation Distance Constraint: min_dist parameter prevents spatial clustering. Points closer distance selected together. value chosen based : Study area size Terrain ruggedness (rugged = smaller min_dist) Typical size soil mapping units
